title: A New Oil Shock Accelerates Return to Nuclear Power
partialText: Shocks to natural gas supplies are spurring countries in Asia and elsewhere to rethink their rejection of nuclear energy after the 2011 disaster in Fukushima, Japan.

title: Jamie Dimon Cites Risks From War, Private Credit, Inflation and More
partialText: In his annual letter to shareholders, Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JPMorgan Chase, said investors and businesses faced a series of challenges.

title: ‘Good to Be Home’: Savannah Guthrie Returns to ‘Today’
partialText: The anchor joined the show’s cast on Monday for the first time since the disappearance of her 84-year-old mother, Nancy, who remains missing.

title: What Does an Ultra-Luxury First Class Ticket Get You? Flying in a Frictionless Bubble.
partialText: A writer reports from inside the premium bubble, where there’s no such thing as too much, petty annoyances are nonexistent and the real world never intrudes.

title: Oil Seesaws After Trump’s Latest Threats on Iran
partialText: President Trump taunted Iranian leaders on Sunday, threatening to escalate attacks if the Strait of Hormuz was not reopened.

title: China Started Preparing for an Energy Crisis Long Before the Iran War
partialText: Long concerned about geopolitical crises, China redoubled efforts to secure energy security when President Trump started raising the stakes in his first term.

title: China Mourned an Education Influencer. The Grief Was a Quiet Revolt.
partialText: Zhang Xuefeng helped people navigate the country’s unforgiving higher education system. The public outpouring after his death was a quiet rebuke to the punishing process.

title: OPEC Plus Warns of Slow Recovery After War in Iran
partialText: The group of influential oil exporters also said it was increasing its production quotas, a largely symbolic move.

title: Despite Poor Reviews, ‘The Super Mario Galaxy Movie’ Is a Megahit
partialText: The animated sequel collected about $373 million worldwide over its first five days in theaters. “Kids love the movie,” a box office analyst said.

title: New Chef Program Helps People With Autism Find Jobs in Fine-Dining Restaurants
partialText: Culinary jobs have the potential to be a perfect fit, and a new effort is afoot to help autistic workers land them.

title: Hockey Rinks Turn to Plastic Ice as Planet Warms
partialText: Some environmentalists question using plastic to address rising temperatures.

title: New Owner of Shopping Plaza in Kansas City Pitches a $1.5 Billion Rescue Plan
partialText: The Country Club Plaza’s sale and turnaround plans come at a consequential economic time for Kansas City, Mo., which will soon lose the Chiefs football team.

title: Oil Markets Doubt Trump’s Peace Signals as Tensions With Iran Grow
partialText: After seesawing between diplomacy and threats, the president may find it harder to knock down prices by suggesting pauses in attacks or progress in talks.

title: Hollywood Writers Union and Studios Reach Contract Deal
partialText: With the global entertainment business reeling during a period of rapid change, there was little enthusiasm on either side for a costly standoff.

title: Orion Samuelson, the Elvis Presley of Agricultural Radio, Dies at 91
partialText: As a host at WGN in Chicago for 60 years, he shared news that was essential to farmers in a homespun style that appealed to listeners from the city.

title: Trump Slashed Science Funding. Now the U.S. Could Face a Costly Brain Drain.
partialText: The White House’s attacks on academia and budget cuts for research have provided an opening for other countries to poach leading scientists.

title: My Husband Can’t Get a Job. Should I Divorce Him?
partialText: Plus, whether to use A.I. to get ahead at work — if you think the technology is evil.

title: Trump Budget Does Little to Address Nation’s Fiscal Challenges
partialText: While the federal deficit has started to shrink under President Trump, his plans could make the long-term situation worse.

title: Some Borrowers Are Moving Abroad and Abandoning Their Student Loans
partialText: A record number of student loan borrowers are in delinquency and default. Some are making the drastic decision to leave the country and abandon their loans.

title: Uber and Lyft Offer Gas Price Relief, but Drivers Say It’s Not Enough
partialText: As fuel costs go up, making a living as a gig driver is harder than ever.

title: ‘I Got Back Every Penny’: Inside Trump’s Supercharged Tax Season
partialText: The law Republicans passed last year has so far been largely imperceptible to most Americans. That’s changing as tens of millions file their taxes this spring.

title: In the Philippines, Rising Fuel Prices Force Travelers to Stay Home During Holy Week
partialText: Surging gasoline prices in the Philippines have forced some people to cancel or scale back the Visita Iglesia, a Holy Week tradition in which Catholics travel to seven churches.

title: ‘Under Protest,’ Raw Dairy Farm Recalls Cheddar Linked to 9 E. Coli Cases
partialText: Raw Farm, a dairy producer in California, denies that its products have caused the outbreak, which has sickened people in three states.

title: United to Offer No-Frills Fares in Its Premium Cabins
partialText: United is introducing restrictive base fares in its most profitable cabins: premium economy and business class.

title: Big Banks Seeking a Piece of SpaceX’s I.P.O. Must Subscribe to Elon Musk’s Grok
partialText: Mr. Musk is requiring Wall Street firms to purchase subscriptions to his A.I. chatbot if they want to advise on one of the largest initial public offerings in history.

title: Why Is the Labor Market Stuck?
partialText: Our chief economics correspondent, Ben Casselman, describes how a “low-hire, low-fire” labor market has left American job-seekers in a bind.

title: What to know about the report.
Parents Who Borrowed for Children’s College Face Looming Deadline
partialText: New rules mean that parent PLUS loans have to be consolidated into a new loan by June 30 for parents to keep affordable payments. But the deadline is really earlier to allow time for processing.

title: Trump Requests $1.5 Trillion for Military Spending
partialText: The huge proposed increase would be partly offset by steep cuts to domestic programs, some of which the Trump administration describes as wasteful.

title: Strong Jobs Numbers Make the Fed’s Job Easier
partialText: Robust job growth in March suggests that the labor market remains relatively healthy, allowing officials at the central bank to focus on fighting inflation.

title: The White House is readying a budget for the statistics agency that compiles the jobs report.
partialText: President Trump is set to release his new spending plan on Friday, after trying last year to cut funding for the federal bureau tasked with measuring the economy.

title: March Jobs Report Shows Stronger U.S. Market Than Expected With 178,000 New Positions
partialText: Payrolls expanded and unemployment dropped last month after a health care strike ended and a harsh winter abated.

title: Economists Are Drawing Stronger Connections Between A.I. and Jobs
partialText: Artificial intelligence hasn’t disrupted the labor market, economists say, but they are increasingly convinced that it will — and that policymakers are unprepared.

title: Skilled Foreign Workers Think About Leaving the U.S.
partialText: As the Trump administration cracks down on the H-1B visa program, which allows skilled workers like software engineers to work in the United States, foreign professionals are debating whether to stay and build careers or quit the American Dream.

title: Jobs and Workers Are In Balance. Nobody Is Happy About It.
partialText: Lower immigration has brought labor supply in line with shaky demand, but economists worry that such a slow-moving job market is at risk of toppling over.

title: How New Yorkers Spend, Splurge and Scrimp to Live in the City
partialText: Eliza Shapiro, who reports on New York City’s affordability crisis, asked hundreds of residents to get candid about their finances.

title: Rival Nations Seize On Choke Points to Counter Trump
partialText: From Iran to China, President Trump’s global aggression has encouraged other countries to search for new ways to pressure the U.S. economy.

title: United Raises Bag Fees, Following JetBlue’s Lead as Fuel Costs Soar
partialText: As the war in Iran strains U.S. airlines, JetBlue and United are now charging up to $10 more for checked bags on domestic flights. More carriers could follow.

title: Hershey’s Promises to Use Only Real Chocolate After Backlash
partialText: The change follows weeks of complaints from a grandson of the Reese’s Peanut Butter Cup inventor and other vocal consumers.

title: Trump Revamps Metal and Pharmaceutical Tariffs
partialText: The administration announced new levies and made changes to existing tariffs for industries that have proved influential on the president’s trade policy.

title: Republicans Seek Protections for Oil Giants Against Climate Lawsuits
partialText: Utah passed a law to insulate oil companies against efforts to make them pay for their role in global warming. A nationwide version is in the works.

title: War With Iran Clarifies Trump’s Spending Priorities: The Military, Not Child Care
partialText: As the White House prepares to release its 2027 budget, President Trump said military protection, not social programs, took precedence.

title: Blue Owl, Ailing Private Credit Firm, Reveals Even More Troubles
partialText: Investors in the struggling Wall Street lender put in record requests to get their money back.

title: Mortgage Rates Climb for 5th Week as Iran War Weighs on U.S. Housing Market
partialText: The average rate on a 30-year mortgage in the United States jumped to 6.46 percent, making it harder for buyers to afford homes.

title: Trump’s Media-Bashing Is Coming Back to Bite Him in Court
partialText: Judges have cited attacks on the press by the president and his appointees when ruling against the government in at least three court cases.

title: Trump Faces a Tough Fight With His New Budget
partialText: Last year, the president proposed many steep spending cuts that Congress never granted. This time, he may face an even tougher sell.

title: Investigators Said to Look at Whether LaGuardia Controller Stepped Away
partialText: Officials are said to be examining whether a controller had to use an emergency phone just before the crash at LaGuardia. They have yet to determine the cause of the crash and are also focusing on other avenues.

title: What the Iran War Could Mean for Stocks, Bonds and Growth
partialText: A merely bad outlook might be good enough for the markets, our columnist says.

title: Tesla Sales Rise as $4-a-Gallon Gas Revives Interest in E.V.s
partialText: The repeal of tax credits last year sent electric vehicle sales plummeting. But with gas prices soaring, consumers are taking another, cautious, look.

title: Why Stocks Tumbled After Trump’s Iran Address
partialText: Oil surged and stocks sold off after the president delivered an unclear case for continuing the war in the Middle East.
